newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products trade hit by weak crude, holiday.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products trade hit by weak crude, holiday.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mostly weakened by the fall in crude futures on Friday, though public holidays thinned business, traders said

Naphtha fell sharply after a selloff in crude oil futures and weaker cargo deals in Northwest Europe on Thursday. But traders said the Med was still the stronger with interest in shipping material to the Far East.

One source said the first four cargoes loading out of Skikda would be double-stems moving east. End-users were holding on to single stem pieces and making it difficult for traders to find two cargoes to load together to make the arbitrage work.
Cargoes were assessed notionally down $5 at $172/$174 cif.
Premium unleaded cargoes fell $2 to $204/$206 due to a drop in futures. Demand from the eastern Med, northern Africa and the U.S., however, has put a floor under prices, traders said.
Gas oil premiums were steady, but sharply lower futures, down $5.50 a tonne, were pulling levels lower.
But 0.2 pct material was seeking, and usually securing, fob high quotes +$3-4 with Russians at similar numbers.
The arb to Singapore, closed earlier in the week, may reopen after the sharp drop, but traders said speculative arbing was unattractive now the main Singapore buyer had quietened down.

Med fuel oil markets were quietened by holidays but some bunker demand needed to be filled and the right grade material looked scarce. Two buyers were chasing material for Las Palmas, with at least one looking at Black Sea straight-runs.
Outright prices for cracked material remained stable, traders said.
One M40 straight-run aboard the Marshal Vasilesky was reported placed, but another, aboard the Irina passed from trader to trader.
